problem: Plassey 1757, Clive, Siraj-ud-daulah, Mir Jafar, diwani 1765 and Permanent Settlement 1793 are supported. But 'about 150 km north of present-day Kolkata' is not in NCERT, and the explanation's 'the majority of the Nawab's army' is not either (NCERT says only that the forces led by Mir Jafar never fought).

fix.answer: In the Battle of Plassey (1757), fought at Palashi, East India Company forces led by Robert Clive defeated Siraj-ud-daulah, the Nawab of Bengal, after Clive had secured the support of his commander Mir Jafar by promising to make him nawab. The Permanent Settlement came into operation in 1793.
fix.explanation: NCERT stresses that the forces led by Mir Jafar never fought the battle. The diwani of Bengal passed to the Company in 1765, between the two events.

Clive had managed to secure his support by promising to make him nawab after crushing Sirajuddaulah.

problem: The first session (1885, Bombay, 72 delegates, Bonnerjee elected president) and the 1907 Surat split are supported. 'Reunited at Lucknow in 1916' is supported by hees202 but contradicted by hess208 (reunion in December 1915; Lucknow Pact in 1916).

fix.answer: The first session of the Indian National Congress was held in Bombay in 1885 with 72 delegates; Womesh Chunder Bonnerjee was elected its first president, and A.O. Hume and Dadabhai Naoroji played leading roles. The Congress split at Surat in 1907; the two groups reunited around 1915-16, and at Lucknow in 1916 the Congress and the Muslim League signed the Lucknow Pact.

quote: Meanwhile, the Congress split in 1907. ... The two groups reunited in December 1915. Next year, the Congress and the Muslim League signed the historic Lucknow Pact
searched: Hume, Naoroji, Bonnerjee, seventy-two delegates (hees202); Surat 1907 (hees202, hess208); Lucknow 1916 and reunion of the two factions (hees202 vs hess208). The two NCERT Class 8 books disagree: Our Pasts III says the groups reunited in December 1915; Exploring Society Part 2 says Tilak's first task (reunion) was achieved in 1916 at the Lucknow session.

Late April 1908, two young members of this group, Khudiram Bose and Prafulla Chaki, tried to assassinate a British judge, Douglas Kingsford, who had been handing down particularly severe sentences to Swadeshi activists ... Khudiram, just 18 years old, was captured, put on trial and hanged a few months later.
